finding: SQLite compound set operators compare raw BLOB carriers instead of logical numeric/byte equality. A real synthetic differential showed UNION duplicated 1 and 1.0, INTERSECT omitted them and EXCEPT retained them in all three dialects.
fix: For compound UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, admit only columns whose possible SQLite carrier classes are statically proven equality-compatible; INTEGER and U64 may compare equal with different carriers, and F64/provider Bytes are unproven. Disjoint INTEGER/U64 versus TEXT/known Bytes are admitted; raw UNION ALL remains unchanged. Original SQL is prepared to distinguish syntax, binding and bare parameter errors before UnsupportedQuery.
supported: NULL, proven INTEGER/Bool, homogeneous U64, Text, or Bytes literal/cast carriers, and pairwise-disjoint class combinations, in direct projections and certain single-table wildcards. Direct length() gives I64/NULL. NativeV1 i64::MIN unary is proven I64; legacy i64::MIN remains unproven due to its F64 intermediate. UNION ALL remains unchanged.
unsupported: F64 including signed zero, mixed INTEGER/U64 carriers, provider Bytes that may include DexMutf8, untyped parameters/derived or other expressions and complex scopes when proof is unavailable. This partial guard prevents known silent wrong rows but does not implement complete compound equality.

red.observation: NativeV1 1 UNION 1.0 yielded 2 rows vs SQLite 1.

red2.observation: All three dialects show wrong rows for UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT; NULL UNION and UNION ALL had no recorded difference. The original red test patch is retained in red2/test.patch.

guard1.observation: Compilation failed: sqlparser VALUES row is Parens; changed iteration to .iter().

param_red.observation: New guard returned UnsupportedQuery for missing bare parameters; corrected using SQLite statement metadata.

param_final2.coverage: bare missing/extra, numbered/named parameters, comments/quoted question marks, CTE and real missing column; sparse ?30000 is bounded by token budget.

mixed3.coverage: single/multi-branch distinct set operators, NULL, F64, Bytes/DexMutf8 rejection, i64 min Native/legacy, U64, disjoint storage classes, bound-scope budget, parameter binding, explicit compound order; includes the new tests.

order_red.observation: Four valid SQLite cases misclassified InvalidArgument in all three dialects. Red test patch retained.

wildcard_red.observation: Existing COMPOUND_WILDCARD_SCHEMA limitation; HEAD source confirms it predates this patch. Test patch retained; no claim of support.

alias_red.observation: Valid SQLite alias from first matching non-leftmost branch misclassified InvalidArgument.

wildcard_middle_red.observation: Ignoring an earlier wildcard arm returned first-column order [7,0,3,2] instead of SQLite [0,2,3,7]; only first dialect/case reached.

case_red.observation: SQLite accepts id+1 ordered by ID+1; bridge reported InvalidArgument.

limits: Synthetic provider and bundled SQLite 3.53.2 only; no actual HostLab/A0/A1, full SQL grammar, full equality, source completeness, Linux or performance qualification. Original DexSQL 0.1.0/0.1.1 behavior was not sampled. NativeV1 signed-min and ordinary INTEGER/TEXT/bytes cases compare SQLite values; U64 ordering/types use explicit hand expectations because SQLite has no native U64 carrier. Native compound TEXT ordering follows UTF-16 and differs from SQLite UTF-8 BINARY for supplementary-plane vs BMP; legacy DexSQL supplementary ordering is unqualified. Carrier proof charges schema entries, parenthesis peeling and repeated scope/alias lookup against shared logical scan budget; existing schema setup, string bytes, allocator/RSS and SQLite memory are outside that bound. Guard may reject previously accepted queries, including floating point, unknown types or mixed INTEGER/U64; complete compound equality remains unimplemented. Complex LEFT BETWEEN and wildcard as the first compound ORDER projection remain unresolved. ORDER proof covers bounded placeholder-free supported AST expression shapes, explicit aliases, and a sole provable single-table wildcard; complex wildcard/unknown scopes are Unsupported after original SQLite verification. Bare parameter metadata validation is added only to these new guard paths; other unsupported paths retain prior boundaries.
order_finding: Valid compound ORDER BY literals, scalar expressions and aliases from later SELECT arms were wrongly rejected because separate AST rewrites produced different bound-parameter slots and the old matching inspected the first arm only. A separate wildcard ORDER query remains an existing unsupported path, as confirmed by HEAD source.
order_fix: Before rewriting a compound SELECT, resolve bounded placeholder-free ORDER expressions or aliases by SQLite left-to-right branch order (each arm aliases before expressions). Proven single-table wildcard expansion is considered; wildcard scopes that cannot be established are checked against original SQL and explicitly unsupported. Identifier/function name comparisons use structured AST with ASCII case-insensitive identifier matching; literals and operators remain exact. Original expression is checked and its temporary internal bindings discarded before substituting the output ordinal. User parameter slots remain independent.
dqs_boundary: A controlled query with an unbound double-quoted identifier is accepted by default SQLite DQS but rejected with SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DQS_DML=false, which is the bridge execution and binding-check configuration. Fixed DexSQL 0.1.0/0.1.1 DQS policy is not established; this is not a legacy equivalence claim.
